title: The Jawbone Siphon
text: At Jawbone Canyon, the Los Angeles Aqueduct dips into the canyon and back out through a pipe 8,095 feet long, with an 850-foot drop. It is the largest of the pressurized tubes along the aqueduct, and its chief engineer, William Mulholland, called this section the Jawbone Siphon. The pipe uses the pressure developed on the downslope to force the water up the far side. It burst in freezing weather in 1988. Europeans who settled the canyon around 1860 named it Jawbone because its shape resembled a mandible.
